links.outcome: Clinician experience, burnout, pajama time, note time, and wRVUs with ambient scribe versus control
links.effect: KLAS Net EHR Experience rose 52.6 to 75.2 in intervention vs 37.3 to 30 in control; burnout fell 89% to 56%; no significant change in pajama time, note time, or wRVUs.
links.quote: Among pediatric subspecialists, AI scribes improved clinician experience and burnout without changing charting time or EHR work outside work hours.

links.outcome: Burnout, documentation time, and wRVUs (coding intensity proxy) after AI scribe deployment
links.effect: Burnout dropped from 8 (89%) to 5 (56%) in intervention; no significant change in time in notes per encounter (+0.2 min) or wRVUs per encounter (-0.03, 95% CI -0.5 to +0.44).
links.quote: There was no significant change to pajama time (-9.4 minutes per scheduled day, 95% CI: -41.2 to +22.4), time in notes per encounter (+0.2 minutes per note, 95% CI: -6.6 to +6.9), or work Relative Value Units (wRVUs) per encounter (-0.03, 95% CI: -0.5 to +0.44).

unlisted_practices: At-the-elbow support for clinicians during ambient scribe rollout

screen.reason: Evaluates the overall deployment impact of an ambient AI scribe tool (Nuance DAX Copilot) on clinician burnout and efficiency via a randomized quality improvement trial, rather than testing a specific safeguard or deployment practice variation.
